angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 333,936 km at 187.17 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.3427 +/- 0.0498 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 187.17 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.48 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-104 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract): 333,936 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.51 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-104 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3712 +/- 54 K from Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-104 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Castro-González et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-104 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-104.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.783, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
